subject.title: fix(mxc): bound sandbox policy file reads to prevent OOM

question: Should OpenClaw accept a fixed 1 MiB maximum for existing MXC sandbox policy files as the compatibility tradeoff for preventing unbounded policy-load memory use?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically sound and preserves symlinked paths, but current users could have an arbitrarily large previously valid policy file; choosing the permanent compatibility boundary is a maintainer policy decision.

options.title: Accept the 1 MiB policy ceiling
options.body: Land the bounded read as proposed, treating policy files above 1 MiB as unsupported so policy loading cannot consume unbounded memory.

options.title: Pause for a different compatibility policy
options.body: Hold the PR if maintainers want a different fixed ceiling or an explicit upgrade plan for oversized existing policy artifacts.

recommendation.title: Accept the 1 MiB policy ceiling
recommendation.body: Land the bounded read as proposed, treating policy files above 1 MiB as unsupported so policy loading cannot consume unbounded memory.
